text: I’ll first check the frozen FS06 B source and analysis, then build an isolated stdio read-window candidate and run focused host semantic tests without touching board resources.

The frozen analysis supports a retained 4096-byte read window, while FS06 B currently invalidates its 64-byte input buffer on every absolute seek. I’m checking allocation, flushing and fd handoff paths now so the window can retain correct positions and ownership.

The candidate can preserve the FILE layout: its allocated read buffer will carry an `off_t` trailer, and unused flag bits will track ownership and position validity. A successful input flush will restore the embedded 64-byte buffer before writes. I also found that the existing update-stream read path calls the flush helper on each read; the active read window needs to bypass that input flush to permit reuse.

The isolated full build is running with FS06 B’s exact configuration and locked local tools. The host tests exercise the actual stdio functions, covering window boundaries, failed seeks and flushes, EOF and pushback, explicit buffers, fd handoff, write transitions, and concurrent stream memory use.

The first host runs passed. In both read-only and update modes, the deterministic 1000-address replay used one data read and two seeks: the initial absolute seek and the one-time position probe. Failure checks also passed with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. The target build completed; I’m now auditing source, dependency and artifact differences.

The remaining audit checks are artifact pairing and source preservation. FILE’s public header is unchanged, but the stdio code is linked into applications, so this candidate needs its matching rebuilt kernel and AppFS. On RV32, each full window requests 4096 bytes plus a 4-byte position trailer; the embedded 64 bytes remain allocated.

The offline audit passed: only the seven intended stdio source files and the new private header differ from frozen B, and all 3343 compile commands match after path normalization. RV32 FILE layout remains identical. The kernel adds 626 bytes of text, with data and BSS unchanged. All 21 application ELFs were rebuilt, and the matching pair is receipted for independent review.

Implemented the isolated candidate in [korvo-fs-stdio-read-window](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-fs-stdio-read-window/README.md), ready for independent review.

- FILE ABI preserved: RV32 `sizeof(FILE)=132`; full window adds **4100 heap bytes plus allocator overhead**, retaining embedded64.
- **184 semantic scenarios pass**, including failures, EOF/ungetc, explicit buffers, cookies/pipes, handoff, writes, ownership and concurrency.
- Host replay: **1000 reads/1000 seeks → 1 read/2 seeks**, plus one fstat/allocation. No board performance claim.
- Clean target build and preservation audit pass. All 3343 compile commands match B; only seven stdio units change. Kernel text **+626 B**, data/BSS unchanged.
- All 21 application ELFs rebuilt; use the matching kernel/AppFS from [final receipt](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-fs-stdio-read-window/final-receipt.json).

Review inputs: [exact patch](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-fs-stdio-read-window/candidate.patch), [audit](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-fs-stdio-read-window/review/review.json), [host results](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-fs-stdio-read-window/host/results.log).

Remaining tradeoffs: retained input lacks coherency with unsynchronized external writers; mixed fd use requires flush/reposition coordination; direction changes release and may later reallocate the window. No hardware resources or maintained/frozen sources were changed.
